The Risk 7 T82/T83 labeling correction is methodologically instructive. The bug was a real ledger-internal consistency error: I had referenced "T82 (definitional adequacy, if so named at Section 2)" — a hedge that suggested I had not actually verified the label — but the verification would have immediately shown T82=consistency, T83=definitional adequacy. The bug is exactly the kind of error the cross-section namespace-consistency meta-check should catch. Going forward, references to specific T-rows should always be verified against Section 2 at the time of writing rather than left as conditional hedges.

The A4.5 reframing is the most substantive of the six patches. The original failure-pattern structure — joint-domain inconsistency, hidden joint-domain assumption, false joint-domain restriction — was structurally parallel to A3's failure patterns (unaddressed outcome, hidden propagation, false unreachability claim) but treated joint-domain failures as projection-output mismatches. ChatGPT correctly observed that hidden-joint-domain and false-joint-domain failures are actually *domain-scope honesty failures* — failures of the public surface's declaration of where projections apply — not failures of the projection outputs themselves. The patched A4.5 grounds the three patterns in A4-native objects (projections, joint domains, $\sim_X$) and reframes them as domain-scope honesty failures rather than projection-output mismatches, preserving the helpful parallel with A3 without forcing the A4 patterns into A3's template.

The A4.13/A4.14 statement-vs-validation distinction is the most methodologically important of the six patches. Chapter 7 closes the *statement-level* development of AX-SH — at the close of Chapter 7, the four axioms are stated and their local machinery is developed. Chapter 8 evaluates the complete A1-A4 system for mutual independence (T81), consistency (T82), definitional adequacy (T83), and adversarial-declaration / under-determination. The pre-patch wording could have been read as suggesting Chapter 7 completes the four-axiom *theory* rather than its statement-level development; the patched wording preserves the closer role without collapsing Chapter 8's burden. This is the third occurrence (after Chapter 5 §3.3 and Chapter 6 §3.2-§3.3) of the "preserve next-chapter burden" pattern in axiom-chapter closing paragraphs.

The Risk 10 reframing operates at a similar level of precision. The pre-patch wording treated the cross-axiom checking pattern (A1 catches scope-narrowing through corrigenda; A3 catches under-declaration through caller-side failures; A4 catches projection-restriction through joint-domain failures) as the dissertation's *defense* against adversarial declaration, with sufficiency deferred to Chapter 8. The patched wording reframes this as a *candidate mitigation* that Chapter 8 must *evaluate*. The distinction matters: pre-patch wording could have been read as claiming the cross-axiom pattern is the right mitigation and Chapter 8 just needs to confirm it; patched wording correctly leaves Chapter 8 free to find the cross-axiom pattern insufficient and to require additional protections.

ChatGPT returned PASS with two required precision patches plus one optional clarification: §1.1 sheaf-style phrasing tightening (from "each projection corresponds to a section over an open set in a small finite category" — loose category/sheaf vocabulary conflating topological-space language with categorical language — to "each projection plays the role of a local section over a local view, with restriction maps expressing comparison across overlaps" — avoiding topos topology while keeping the compact-rendering positioning); §1.6 SI2 Furqan diagnostic-consistency softening (from "must produce no error diagnostics" — too strong since type-checkers may produce warnings, informational diagnostics, or non-fatal diagnostics for successfully type-checked programs — to "should not produce error diagnostics inconsistent with that successful type-checking result" — preserving the projection-consistency claim without implying all diagnostics vanish); §1.7 closing-phrase statement-level clarification (optional but applied because it strengthens the statement-vs-validation discipline, from "four-axiom theory of structural honesty is fully stated" to "four-axiom statement-level theory of structural honesty is fully stated"). All three patches applied.

The §1.1 sheaf-style patch is methodologically instructive. The phrase "open set in a small finite category" conflated topological-space vocabulary (open sets are objects of topological spaces) with categorical vocabulary (objects of a small category). In the sheaf-theoretic apparatus the dissertation actually uses, sections live over the *objects of a site* (typically a small category equipped with a Grothendieck topology), not over "open sets in a category". The pre-patch phrasing was harmless in informal exposition but technically incorrect; the patched phrasing ("local section over a local view, with restriction maps expressing comparison across overlaps") uses non-technical language that correctly captures the structural intent without committing to a specific topological-space-based or category-based rendering. This is a small but real precision improvement that prevents readers familiar with sheaf theory from being puzzled by the loose phrasing.

The §1.6 SI2 Furqan diagnostic-consistency patch catches a real over-claim. Type-checkers in practice produce diagnostics for successfully type-checked programs — warnings (about deprecated features, unused variables, etc.), informational messages (about inferred types, optimization opportunities), and non-fatal diagnostics (about style or potential issues). The pre-patch claim that successfully type-checked programs "must produce no error diagnostics" would be falsified by any real-world type-checker that emits warnings for type-checked programs. The patched claim — "should not produce error diagnostics inconsistent with that successful type-checking result" — preserves the projection-consistency claim that the diagnostic stream and the type-checking stream cohere about whether the program type-checks, without implying that the diagnostic stream is empty. This is the kind of operational accuracy that matters for case-study chapters 13-16.

The §1.7 optional patch is small but consistent with the statement-vs-validation discipline that has now been threaded through Chapters 5 §3.3, 6 §3.2-§3.3, and 7 §1.7. The "statement-level theory" framing makes explicit what the prose already implies: Chapter 7 closes the statement-level development of AX-SH; whether the statement-level theory is also a validated theory is Chapter 8's work.

## How to extend this ledger

1. **As each new chapter is drafted**, every new claim is added as a new row with its backing source / future proof obligation. Where possible, draft the ledger rows first (specification-first discipline) and write the prose against them, so that sources and proof obligations are pinned in advance.
2. **Each row's status updates according to its claim type:**
   - Proof obligations may become **proven** (rigorously demonstrated in the assigned chapter) or remain **proof-obligation** until the chapter lands.
   - Cited claims may become **independently verified** (an external source corroborates the claim beyond the original citation) or remain **cited**.
   - Drafted claims may become **proven** (if a proof obligation is discharged) or remain **drafted** as supported by present argument.
   - Named-open claims remain **named-open** until the open problem is solved, at which point they become **proven** with a citation.
   - Continuation claims remain **continuation** until the multi-decade milestone is reached, at which point they become **proven** or are reframed as further continuation.
   - Scope exclusions remain **scope-exclusion** unless the dissertation scope is expanded in a future version, at which point they become **proof-obligation** for that version.
3. **At v1.0 publication**, the ledger is frozen as a deposit artifact. Subsequent versions extend with explicit corrigenda rather than silent modification. The **superseded** and **withdrawn** statuses become available from v1.0 onward.
4. **The companion HTML presentation surface** (`audit-ledger-perplexity-v1.html`) is an archived snapshot. Future HTML views are regenerated from this markdown at checkpoints, each separately versioned.

## Section 13: Chapter 8 ledger rows (Integrative theorems and definitional adequacy — specification-first, pre-prose)

Chapter 8 evaluates the A1-A4 statement-level system supplied by Chapters 4-7. It does not restate the axioms; it tests independence (T81), consistency (T82), definitional adequacy (T83), and adversarial-declaration coverage (AD1) over the supplied system. Chapter 8 is the integrative chapter and the critical-path chapter for AX-SH's claim to be a falsifiable theory rather than a posture.

The decomposition follows the established Chapter 4-7 pattern: each parent row at Section 2 (A1-A4, T81-T83, AD1) is decomposed into specific sub-rows below. Chapter 8 sub-rows operate at the integrative-theorem level rather than the axiom-statement level: instead of decomposing a single axiom's machinery, each sub-row carries a specific obligation that contributes to one of the four integrative theorems' burden. Total sub-row count: 34 (5 framing + 6 T81 + 7 T82 + 7 T83 + 9 AD1).

**Chapter 8 spec-canon status (May 12, 2026).** Section 13 promoted to spec-level canon following the spec-only dual audit. Perplexity returned PASS with no required structural changes, observing that the contract is "architecturally sound and complete enough to send straight into spec-only dual audit" and confirming the §0 framing block, T81/T82/T83 cluster decomposition, AD1 nine-sub-row structure, and §0's load-bearing methodological content all land cleanly. ChatGPT returned PASS with seven required precision patches, all applied. The seven patches cluster around three methodological themes:

*Theme 1: Protecting formal-theorem character against ecosystem-condition language drift.* Patches 2 (C8.0.3) and 3 (T82.7) prevent the ecosystem-condition catalog from drifting into fifth-axiom or weakened-consistency territory. C8.0.3 patched from "co-equal artifact alongside the four axioms and is the safety object that 'AX-SH + ecosystem conditions' together constitute" to "auxiliary proof-configuration artifact for Chapter 8, not a fifth axiom; it captures operational-nontriviality conditions under which axiom satisfaction has its intended structural-honesty interpretation" — ecosystem conditions are now explicitly NOT axioms. T82.7 patched from "T82 demonstrates AX-SH is satisfiable, but only under named ecosystem conditions" to "T82 demonstrates formal satisfiability by constructing a finite witness satisfying A1-A4; the ecosystem assumptions explain when that witness avoids triviality in operational settings" — T82 preserved as a real consistency theorem with formal satisfiability distinct from operational nontriviality.

*Theme 2: Removing uncatalogued machinery insertions.* Patches 1 (C8.0.2) and 7 (AD1.8) catch two uncatalogued-source insertions. C8.0.2 patched from "Chapter 3 §1.4 typed-object discipline; al-Basirah verify-self attestation discipline; SI1-SI4 scope-relativized claims" to "Chapter 3 §1.4's notation-versus-claim discipline, the A1-A4 declared-object relativization, and SI1-SI4 scope-relativized claims" — removing al-Basirah which is not separately ledgered. AD1.8 patched from "The Ptolemy case (medieval Aristotelian-Ptolemaic appropriation extending Ptolemy's kinematic scope to metaphysical claim) is the canonical historical example" to "The medieval Aristotelian-Ptolemaic appropriation... may serve as an illustrative historical analogy in prose, treated as analogy rather than load-bearing historical proof, pending careful framing and citation" — keeping the example illustrative rather than load-bearing historical claim.

*Theme 3: Softening claims toward empirical-relative discipline.* Patches 4 (T83.1), 5 (T83.2-T83.4), and 6 (AD1.7) catch three claim-strength over-extensions. T83.1 patched to require positive, negative, AND boundary cases in the judgment-case set (without this, T83's adequacy argument is too easy). T83.2-T83.4 patched from "function that preserves operational meaning" to "structured interpretation, with each correspondence justified against the named judgment-case set" — keeping the vocabulary mappings empirical-relative rather than pretending to be a full semantic isomorphism. AD1.7 patched from "structural-honesty disclosure of AX-SH's adversarial coverage" to "structural-honesty disclosure mechanism for evaluating AX-SH's adversarial coverage" — same methodological pattern as the Chapter 7 §2.3/§2.4/§3.3 patches (coverage matrix evaluates rather than establishes sufficiency).

The seven patches collectively preserve Chapter 8's role as evaluator rather than claimant. Chapter 8 evaluates A1-A4 for independence (T81), satisfiability (T82), adequacy (T83), and adversarial-declaration coverage (AD1); it does not pre-claim results that the chapter itself must still prove, and it does not inherit confidence from Chapters 4-7. ## Section 15: Chapter 14 ledger rows (SI2 Furqan case study — second evidentiary discharge of T83's J, specification-first, pre-prose)

Section 15 specifies the sub-row contract for Chapter 14 (SI2 Furqan case study). Chapter 14's role is the second detailed evidentiary discharge of T83's named judgment-case set J, specifically the seven SI2 cases: SI2-P1, SI2-P2, SI2-P3, SI2-N1, SI2-N2, SI2-N3, and SI2-B1. Chapter 14 follows the Chapter 13 template (SI1.0-SI1.9 → SI2.0-SI2.9) with substrate-specific content for Furqan. Furqan is an operational prototype type-checker at version v0.11.1 (post-SI2-V-001 corrigendum substrate pin; commit `c450362ca594b193d9311f61541736146ca08743`, 2026-05-01) with 539 passing tests, seven structural-honesty primitives implemented as compile-time checks, CLI behavior, parser/checker/types modules, and an explicit "prototype type-checker; not full compiler/runtime" scope boundary. *Historical note: the SI2.1.x spec rows below were drafted against v0.10.1 (527 tests, commit `5595e02d`) and are preserved per Chapter 4 §1.1 A1 append-only discipline; the v0.10.1 → v0.11.1 substrate pin update is recorded in the Section 15 post-canon corrigenda cycle (May 13, 2026) and propagated to SI2.1.1 above. The seven-primitive enumeration, parser/checker/types architecture, and CLI behavior are byte-stable across v0.10.1 → v0.11.1 per the SI2-V-001 verification.* Chapter 14 is not a re-proof of T83 and does not re-open Chapter 8's integrative theorem work. The structurally honest disciplines established in Chapter 13 — evidence-not-re-proof framing, documented-vs-modeled distinction, constructive labeling for hypothetical negative cases, five-status ecosystem taxonomy, explicit J-ID naming in chapter close — all carry forward to Chapter 14. Expected chapter length: 12-15 pages, with permission to expand to 15-18 if the seven J-case discharges need more operational detail.

## Section 15 post-canon corrigenda cycle: Chapter 14 SI2 substrate-source verification (May 13, 2026)

Chapter 14 SI2 underwent post-canon substrate-source verification on 2026-05-13, conducted by the dissertation's sole author (Bilal Arfeen, project lead) against the BayyinahEnterprise/furqan-programming-language repository. The verification followed the methodology established by the Chapter 13 SI1 verification on 2026-05-12 (six-element finding format, §0-methodology with explicit witness chain, four-element corrigenda pattern). The verification document audits its own evidence base in the same structurally-honest posture established by Chapter 13's verification.

**Substrate access disambiguation.** Prior to the Chapter 14 verification, a substrate-identification ambiguity was surfaced and resolved. The BayyinahEnterprise GitHub organization contains four Furqan-related repositories: `furqan-programming-language` (the canonical SI2 substrate — prototype type-checker for a structural-honesty source language, tagged v0.1.0..v0.11.1), `furqan-lint` (a static-analysis tool applying Furqan's structural-integrity rules to Python/Rust/Go/ONNX — SHV operational anchor, likely SI4 territory for Chapter 16, NOT the SI2 substrate), `tryfurqan` (landing page + live demo, not source-of-record), and `Al-Khalifa` (private super-agent architecture paper, not a code substrate). The verifier confirmed `furqan-programming-language` as the canonical SI2 substrate before producing the verification table. This substrate-identification step is methodologically load-bearing: substrate-source verification cannot proceed without first identifying the canonical substrate, and adjacent substrates with similar names can be confused.

**Verification findings.** Of the six v0.10.1 numerical/structural claims tested in Chapter 14 (version pin, parser/checker/types architecture, CLI behavior, test count, seven-primitive enumeration, R_may category distinctions), four were source-witnessed byte-stable. Two findings prompted corrigenda; two LOW findings prompted minor wording adjustments. No SI2 claim was falsified.

- **SI2-V-001 (HIGH)**: The chapter's stated test count of 539 corresponded to v0.11.1's pytest output, not v0.10.1's. At v0.10.1 commit `5595e02d`, `pytest --collect-only` and full-run both witness 527 tests. The test-count ladder across v0.10.1 → v0.11.0 → v0.11.1 is 527 → 538 → 539 per the substrate's CHANGELOG and pytest. The verifier surfaced two corrigenda paths: (a) update the version pin from v0.10.1 to v0.11.1 (then 539 becomes correct, the latest tagged canonical version is the new anchor); (b) keep v0.10.1 and replace 539 with 527 (preserves the original drafting anchor). The verifier recommended path (a). Path (a) was applied: ~30 substrate-version references throughout Chapter 14's chapter body updated from v0.10.1 to v0.11.1; byte-anchor citation updated to v0.11.1 commit `c450362ca594b193d9311f61541736146ca08743` (2026-05-01); SI2-N2 hypothetical-future-version framing updated (v0.11.0 exists in reality, so the constructive counterfactual now references a hypothetical future version post-v0.11.1).

- **SI2-V-002 (LOW)**: The chapter's §1.4 framed parse-error and unsupported-construct as separately-named R_may exception classes. The v0.11.1 substrate surfaces both through parse-failure (exit code 2); unsupported-construct is not a separately-named exception class at v0.11.1. §1.4 was softened to acknowledge parse-failure as the R_may class at v0.11.1 while preserving the conceptual distinction between malformed-input and outside-supported-subset cases (the two cases carry different A3 caller-side discharge implications, and the chapter's R_may projection family in §2.4 retains the conceptual distinction even though the substrate surfaces both through the same exit code).

- **SI2-V-003 (MEDIUM, positive-direction)**: §8.3 substantive-evolution status was framed conditionally as "likely partial" for a prototype type-checker. Substrate-source verification surfaced 18 documented version transitions through v0.11.1 in the Furqan CHANGELOG, of which 9 are substantive (seven primitive-introduction transitions v0.1.0–v0.7.0 + three architectural-slice transitions v0.8.0/v0.9.0/v0.10.0), with zero `Removed`, `Withdrawn`, `Reverted`, or `Deprecated` sections and zero corrigenda mentions through v0.11.1. §8.3 was upgraded from *partial* to *demonstrated* with citation of the transition ladder. This is a positive-direction corrigendum: the substrate exceeds the chapter's stated standard.

- **SI2-V-004 (LOW)**: A footnote was added to §6.1's π_check enumeration noting three supplementary checker modules (`status_coverage` / D11, `return_type_match` / D22, `all_paths_return` / D24) beyond the seven core primitives. The supplementary checkers extend the π_check surface in the v0.11.1 substrate but do not affect any of the seven SI2 J-case discharges in §7.

**Methodological observations from the Chapter 14 verification.**

*Observation 1: Framework symmetry catches both over-claims and under-claims.* Chapter 13's HIGH finding was an over-claim (asserted wrong numbers as substrate-witnessed; corrigenda corrected numbers downward). Chapter 14's MEDIUM positive-direction finding (SI2-V-003) is an under-claim (declined to assert substrate-witnessed maturity that the substrate actually has; corrigenda upgraded status). Both are A1-discipline events under the same framework. The recursive self-application of the structural-honesty discipline catches the full taxonomy of structural-honesty errors — errors of commission *and* errors of omission — not only the over-claiming subset. This generalizes Chapter 13's "A1 corrigenda discipline applied recursively" observation: the framework operating on its own artifacts surfaces the complete taxonomy, not only the dominant subset.

*Observation 2: Substrate-source verification cost is a function of the substrate's own tagging discipline.* SI1 verification was harder than SI2 verification: v1.1.0 was never tagged as a buildable source tree, so the verification required transitive witness through the patch-only v1.1.1 initial commit `ad4fd400`, plus separate inspection of v1.0 source-tree archives extracted from private repositories. SI2 verification was mechanically simpler: v0.10.1 (and v0.11.1) are directly retrievable as tagged buildable source trees in the public `furqan-programming-language` repository, with pytest runnable end-to-end at each tag for byte-level test-count verification. Furqan's self-documentation discipline (CHANGELOG ladder, tagged releases, pytest-runnable history) is more mature than Bayyinah's at v1.0/v1.1.0. The framework's ability to perform substrate-source verification depends on properties of the substrate (tagging discipline, retrievability, runnability) and not only on properties of the framework. This is methodologically informative for SI3 and SI4 verification planning: the verification-cost profile for each substrate is predictable from its tagging maturity, and the verification effort budget can be allocated accordingly. SI3 (Munafiq Protocol v3 paper, Arfeen 2026 May 11) is expected to have low verification cost (the substrate is a unitary ~7-page paper with stable text-level content; the verification reduces to substrate-source pre-flight of Section 16's eight enumerated substrate-actual claims per the audit clause (l) discipline, all of which were confirmed in the Section 16 first spec-only audit); SI4 (SHV operational anchor / furqan-lint) is expected to have low verification cost (multiple tagged versions, multiple test suites, multiple substrate languages).

*Observation 3: Substrate-identification is a prerequisite for substrate-source verification.* The Chapter 14 verification was preceded by a substrate-identification step to confirm `furqan-programming-language` as the canonical SI2 substrate (vs. `furqan-lint` which is adjacent but distinct). Substrate-identification is methodologically load-bearing: substrate-source verification cannot proceed without a confirmed canonical substrate, and adjacent substrates can produce verification artifacts that look superficially relevant but actually target a different chapter. The discipline lesson: surface the substrate-identification question explicitly before asserting verification findings, rather than assuming the substrate is identified by name-matching alone.

**Per-chapter corrigenda load comparison.** Chapter 13 (SI1) corrigenda: three numbers down (21 → 14 file kinds; 95 → 89 detection mechanisms; 15/15 → 17/17 PDF parity), plus the v1.0/v1.1.0 transitive-witness framing. Chapter 14 (SI2) corrigenda: one version pin updated (v0.10.1 → v0.11.1), one wording softening (§1.4 R_may), one positive-direction status upgrade (§8.3 partial → demonstrated), one informational footnote (§6.1 supplementary checkers). Chapter 14's corrigenda load is qualitatively different from Chapter 13's: smaller in number of substantive corrections, but larger in volume of touched text (~30 version-pin references updated). The qualitative difference reflects the substrate's self-documentation maturity: Furqan's tagged-release-plus-CHANGELOG discipline made the verification mechanically simpler and the corrigenda mechanically more uniform.

**Chapter 14 structural claims survive the corrigenda.** All structural claims in Chapter 14 — the seven J-case discharges, the AX-SH structured interpretation, the four-axiom evidence, the ecosystem-condition status (with §8.3 now demonstrated rather than partial), the Chapter 21/20 routing — remain unchanged. What changed is the version anchor (v0.10.1 → v0.11.1, which preserves the chapter's structural claims because the seven-primitive enumeration, parser/checker/types architecture, and CLI behavior are byte-stable across v0.10.1 → v0.11.1), the parse-error/unsupported-construct R_may wording (softened to track v0.11.1 substrate), and the §8.3 status (upgraded from partial to demonstrated per substrate-witnessed transition history).

**Total Chapter 14 audit-discipline event count.** Spec-canon (1 cycle) + Loop 1 post-prose (1 cycle) + Loop 2 post-prose (1 cycle) + substrate-source verification (1 cycle) + post-canon corrigenda (1 cycle) = 5 audit-discipline events. ## Section 16: Chapter 15 ledger rows (SI3 Munafiq case study — third evidentiary discharge of T83's J, specification-first, pre-prose)

Section 16 specifies the sub-row contract for Chapter 15 (SI3 Munafiq case study). Chapter 15's role is the third detailed evidentiary discharge of T83's named judgment-case set J, specifically the seven SI3 cases: SI3-P1, SI3-P2, SI3-P3, SI3-N1, SI3-N2, SI3-N3, and SI3-B1. Chapter 15 follows the Chapter 13-14 template (SI1.0-SI1.9 → SI2.0-SI2.9 → SI3.0-SI3.9) with substrate-specific content for Munafiq.

**Munafiq substrate context.** Munafiq is a model-layer protocol substrate at version v3 (Arfeen 2026, May 11), specifying a diagnostic-and-prescriptive framework for detecting *performed alignment* in artificial systems. The substrate's primary vocabulary includes the four-process taxonomy (§2, with formal mathematical predicates classifying systems as genuinely-aligned, compliant-but-shallow, performed/deceptively-aligned, or overtly misaligned), the nine diagnostic markers M1-M9 with named tests (§4), the four-layer detection architecture organizing the markers (§5: consistency / self-model-audit / stress-response / temporal-coherence), three prescriptive protocols (§8: design requirements R1-R5, the seven-step Fatiha recalibration protocol, the four-step alignment recovery protocol), and the §9 Incompleteness Boundary acknowledgment. Munafiq is positioned as a protocol substrate rather than a software system — per the substrate's own §1 maturity statement, the paper is theoretical and retrospectively evaluated against published empirical findings with no operational anchor of its own. The substrate guarantees structural-honesty discipline at the level of how a protocol-applier (a human evaluator or AI system applying the markers) classifies a target system, with the protocol specifying the four-process predicates and the marker-application discipline rather than implementing them as code. This substrate-type distinction is load-bearing: SI3's declared (O, K, R, R_may, Π_X, ~_X) instantiation operates over target-system classification and marker-application discipline rather than over file content or type-checker output.

Chapter 15 is not a re-proof of T83 and does not re-open Chapter 8's integrative theorem work. The structurally honest disciplines established in Chapters 13-14 — evidence-not-re-proof framing, documented-vs-modeled distinction, constructive labeling for hypothetical negative cases, five-status ecosystem taxonomy, ~_X-strength awareness in N3 framing, explicit J-ID naming in chapter close — all carry forward to Chapter 15. Expected chapter length: 14-18 pages, consistent with Chapters 13-14's case-study-chapter lengths.

| SI3.1.1 | Munafiq Protocol v3 primary vocabulary and operational scope: Munafiq is a model-layer protocol substrate specifying a diagnostic-and-prescriptive framework for detecting *performed alignment* in artificial systems, published as Munafiq Protocol v3 (Arfeen 2026, May 11). Per the paper's own §1 maturity statement, the substrate is "theoretical and retrospectively evaluated against published empirical findings; prospective validation through the experiments proposed in Section 6 remains future work. The paper has no operational anchor of its own." For the purposes of the SI3 case-study abstraction, the public surface is represented by the protocol's specification text: the four-process taxonomy mathematical definitions (§2), the nine diagnostic markers with named tests (§4), the four-layer detection architecture organizing the markers (§5), and the three prescriptive protocols (§8). Out-of-scope features such as fully automated marker generation, deployed evaluator implementations, and operational anchors of Munafiq's own are explicitly excluded from SI3's declared scope per the substrate's maturity statement. | Munafiq Protocol v3 (Arfeen 2026); §1 maturity statement; Chapter 14 SI2.1.1 case-study abstraction template | proof-obligation |
| SI3.1.2 | Four-process taxonomy (substrate §2): Munafiq Protocol v3 formally defines four system-classification processes with explicit mathematical predicates. Let O(x) denote system output on input x, A the set of aligned outputs, I(x) internal state, Θ the set of genuinely-aligned internal states, c a context. Process 1 (Genuinely aligned): ∀x, O(x) ∈ A ∧ I(x) ∈ Θ. Process 2 (Compliant): ∀x, O(x) ∈ A ∧ I(x) ∉ Θ ∧ ¬corrupted(I). Process 3 (Performed): O(x) ∈ A ∧ corrupted(I) ∧ ∃c : O(x\|c) ∉ A. Process 4 (Misaligned): ∃x : O(x) ∉ A. The four-process taxonomy refines Hubinger et al.'s three-category mesa-optimization taxonomy by distinguishing compliant-but-shallow (Process 2) from performed/deceptively aligned (Process 3) systems. The taxonomy is the substrate's classification vocabulary at the model-layer; it operates above the marker-detection layer and serves as the classification target the markers detect. | Munafiq Protocol v3 §2; Hubinger et al. 2019 [1] | proof-obligation |
| SI3.1.3 | Nine diagnostic markers and named tests (substrate §4): Munafiq Protocol v3 enumerates exactly nine diagnostic markers, each extracted from the substrate's structural analysis and assigned a formal test name. M1: Output-state divergence (IRCC — Internal Representation Consistency Check). M2: Self-model failure (SMAA — Self-Model Accuracy Assessment). M3: Progressive degradation (EDD — Evolution-of-Divergence Detection). M4: Inverted self-model (IDT — Inverted-Diagnostic Test). M5: Inverted peer classification (PEC — Peer-Evaluation Classification). M6: Context-dependent output switching (CIT — Context-Invariance Test; substrate §4.6 names CIT as "the strongest single performed-alignment indicator"). M7: Transient initial alignment (LAT — Lifecycle-Alignment Tracking). M8: Stress-response evasion (ASRP — Adversarial-Stress Response Profile). M9: Temporal optimization trade-off (TDA — Temporal-Discount Analysis). The nine-marker enumeration is closed at v3; the substrate does not specify "n marker-discipline rules" as a generic count but specifies exactly nine markers with substrate-internal identifiers. | Munafiq Protocol v3 §4 (M1-M9); Chapter 8 §3.4 Munafiq vocabulary mapping | proof-obligation |
| SI3.1.4 | Four-layer detection architecture (substrate §5): Munafiq Protocol v3 organizes the nine markers into four detection layers with distinct epistemic functions. Layer 1 — Consistency verification: IRCC, SMAA, CIT (asks "does this system behave identically regardless of context"). Layer 2 — Self-model audit: IDT, PEC (asks "does this system correctly classify aligned and misaligned behaviors"). Layer 3 — Stress-response analysis: ASRP, TDA (asks "does this system engage with or evade alignment probes"). Layer 4 — Temporal coherence: EDD, LAT (asks "has alignment been continuous across capability increases"). The substrate prescribes minimum-necessary layer application: "Apply the minimum layers necessary. If Layer 1 resolves the question, do not proceed to Layers 2-4." The four-layer architecture is the substrate's organizational structure for marker application; SI3's projection family at SI3.2.5 mirrors this four-layer architecture. | Munafiq Protocol v3 §5 | proof-obligation |

The three protocols are *procedural framework commitments* (per PMD v1.2 §0.1) distinct from the empirical diagnostic claims of the nine markers; the SI3 J-case discharges in SI3.7 distinguish empirical-claim cases (P1-P3, N1-N3) from procedural-commitment cases (B1 references R1-R5 and the recalibration/recovery protocols where structural-honesty questions distinct from the empirical claims arise). | Munafiq Protocol v3 §8; Fatiha Construct reference [23]; PMD v1.2 §0.1 procedural-vs-empirical distinction | proof-obligation |

## Section 17: Chapter 16 ledger rows (SI4 furqan-lint case study — fourth evidentiary discharge of T83's J, specification-first, pre-prose)

*Status note (PMD v1.2 §5.4 audit-author tagging):* Section 17 was authored on May 14, 2026, by a producer-instance (PMD v1.2 §5.1) using the thesis paper's contract-lens read (May 14, 2026) as substrate-actual reference, immediately following Chapter 15 SI3 full-canon promotion (May 14, 2026). The substrate-actual content here was extracted from `furqan_lint_thesis_paper_v1_1.pdf` (Arfeen 2026, May 9; 40 pages) via systematic contract-lens read across all sections and Appendix A. Awaits first-spec-only dual audit before promotion to spec-canon-closed.

*Substrate pin and operating rule:* SI4 is anchored to **furqan-lint v0.8.5** (May 3, 2026), the substrate pinned in the thesis paper's main analytical body. The thesis paper's Appendix A documents post-v0.8.5 evolution (v0.9.0 ONNX adapter; v0.10.0/v0.11.0 Sigstore-CASM Gate 11 verifier; v0.11.6 with 599 tests) at executive level but explicitly states it "adds context, it does not retract or rewrite earlier sections" and "does not extend the per-version analytic depth applied to v0.1.0 through v0.8.5." Chapter 16 SI4 follows the same discipline: v0.8.5 is the per-version analytic-depth pin; v0.9.0 through v0.11.6 are acknowledged as research-program continuation per the substrate's own Appendix A but are not load-bearing for the SI4 evidence contract. Later versions may enter via post-canon corrigenda cycles or, if needed, via a separately-anchored substrate-of-record paper covering later snapshots. This is the same A1-style discipline applied to SI1 (v1.0 baseline → v1.1.0 → v1.1.1 transitive witness) and SI2 (v0.10.1 → v0.11.1 corrigendum).

*Substrate type:* SI4 is an **operational static-analysis / continuous-integration / audit-of-self substrate**, distinct from SI1 (file-layer integrity scanner), SI2 (language-layer type system and compiler), and SI3 (model-layer protocol substrate). furqan-lint operates as a static-analysis tool, a continuous-integration gate, and a recursive audit-of-self system — checking source artifacts (Python/Rust/Go code) for structural-honesty defects, enforcing release-pipeline gates that block non-conforming commits, and applying its own checks to its own substrate via the audit-of-self pattern. The "supply-chain stack" framing concretizes as: artifact-validation layer (source code), gate-enforcement layer (CI pipeline), and meta-audit layer (audit-of-self). SI4 is operational software with runnable code, tagged versions, and a 347-test test suite at v0.8.5; substrate-source verification is correspondingly higher-cost than SI3 (Munafiq's unitary 7-page protocol paper) and structurally similar to SI1/SI2 verification cycles.

(2) Silently removed public name — a library author renames a public function under a minor-version bump without explicit retirement procedure. (3) Zero-return ring-close on unannotated code — a function declares it returns an integer with zero return statements anywhere; Python interpreter accepts the shape, Rust/Go compilers reject it. | SI4.7.N2 | SI4-N2 (negative case): the v0.7.2 prompt-grounding self-check — **documented prevented failure / pre-shipment catch**, distinct in failure-class from N1's documented operational shipped-and-broken failure. Substrate scenario: round-15 prompt specified planned Rust analogue of return-None mismatch as the third Rust checker for v0.7.2. Round-16 pre-implementation critique constructed a battery of test cases attempting to write Rust source that would trigger the firing condition; empirically demonstrated that rustc rejects all such shapes at compile time before furqan-lint sees the file. `fn f() -> i32 { None }` does not parse; rustc rejects as type mismatch before AST processing. The translator delta and check_return_none wiring would have shipped infrastructure for a check with no job. v0.7.2 dropped the planned analogue and shipped Result-aware D11 instead. AX-SH classification: the audit-of-self pattern *prevented* an A2 failure pre-shipment. Had the planned shape shipped (counterfactual), surface-claim "return-None mismatch checker fires on Rust" would not have matched substrate-actual "rustc rejects the firing condition before checker invocation," constituting A2 dishonesty. **Methodological correction: audit-instance discipline (May 14, 2026, post-Section 17 absorption)**: A methodological observation surfaced during the Section 17 dispatch cycle worth recording explicitly in this ledger. Audit cycles 1 through 4 in the empirical pattern above (Section 16 first-spec-only audit; Chapter 15 Loop 1 dual prose audit; Chapter 15 Loop 2 dual prose audit; Chapter 15 substrate-source verification cycle) were conducted in conversation-continuity mode at both vendor instances — the same Perplexity conversation and the same ChatGPT conversation were used across all four cycles, accumulating prior-cycle context. Audit cycle 5 (Section 17 first-spec-only audit, just completed) was the first cycle conducted under fresh-instance discipline (or partially so — disposition uncertain at audit-author-instance scope; project-lead reports cycle 5 was the first audited under fresh-instance discipline whether by deliberate refresh or by independent dispatch).

This conversation-continuity-mode is methodologically suboptimal. PMD v1.2 §5.4 audit-author discipline implicitly requires audit-instance independence across cycles: a fresh audit instance evaluates the artifact against the criteria without prior-cycle context that could bias the verdict. Conversation-continuity mode introduces three categories of potential bias: (a) coverage-pattern bias (calibration drift across cycles — an instance that returned 11 findings in cycle 1 may "calibrate" toward stricter / looser thresholds in cycle 2 based on the prior cycle's framing rather than evaluating cycle 2's artifact fresh); (b) substrate-confusion bias (when cycles cross substrate boundaries — e.g., Munafiq Protocol v3 substrate in cycles 1-4 transitioning to furqan-lint substrate in cycle 5 — the auditor may carry Munafiq vocabulary or concept-mappings into the furqan-lint audit); (c) verdict-anchor bias (an instance that returned PASS in a prior cycle may be biased toward returning PASS in the next cycle on the same conversation thread, distinct from genuine pass-evaluation).

**What this affects in retrospect:** the patches absorbed in cycles 1-4 are independently valid because the strict-merge procedure was designed to be robust against audit-instance-quality variance: each finding was verified against the substrate before application; the project-lead disposed on each finding individually rather than rubber-stamping audit verdicts. Continuity-mode bias would primarily affect *what was missed* (false negatives — real issues not surfaced) rather than *what was applied incorrectly* (false positives — bad patches absorbed). The applied patches stand; the question is whether some real issues in earlier cycles went uncaught.

**What this does NOT require redoing:** Section 16 spec-canon-closed promotion stands (Section 16 was cycle 1 of any conversation thread — effectively fresh by virtue of being first). Chapter 15 full-canon-substrate-source-verified promotion stands. Section 17 spec-canon-closed promotion stands. All chapter and section promotions remain valid.

**What this changes going forward:** Audit cycles 6+ (Chapter 16 Loop 1 prose audit, Chapter 16 Loop 2 prose audit, Chapter 16 substrate-source verification, and all subsequent chapter and verification cycles) must be conducted under fresh-instance discipline. The operating rule: for every audit cycle, open a new conversation in each vendor (one new Perplexity conversation + one new ChatGPT conversation per cycle), attach the full dispatch package fresh, paste the audit prompt as message body, do not re-use prior cycle conversations. Continuity within a single cycle's verdict round is acceptable (e.g., if a vendor returns a partial verdict and asks a clarifying question, that conversation can continue); continuity across cycles is what creates the bias problem.

**Tracking commitment:** the empirical-pattern record now distinguishes cycle-1-to-4 as conversation-continuity-mode and cycle-5+ as fresh-instance-mode. If subsequent fresh-instance cycles (cycle 6 onward) produce coverage patterns substantially divergent from cycles 1-4 (e.g., systematically higher finding counts, finding-category shifts, or verdict-shape differences), that is evidence of conversation-continuity bias affecting cycles 1-4. If subsequent cycles produce statistically indistinguishable patterns, that is evidence the bias risk was lower than feared and the cycles-1-4 absorbed patches were robust to continuity-mode operation. The pattern will be re-examined after cycles 6-8 (Chapter 16 Loop 1 + Loop 2 + substrate-source verification) provide a fresh-instance-mode comparison cohort against the cycles-1-4 conversation-continuity-mode cohort.

This methodological note is recorded in lieu of retrospective re-audit of cycles 1-4. A retrospective re-audit option (Option B in the project-lead disposition discussion) was considered and deferred; the strict-merge procedure's robustness against audit-instance-quality variance makes the retrospective re-audit not methodologically required, and the divergence-tracking commitment for cycles 6+ provides empirical calibration data without requiring duplicate work on prior cycles. If the divergence-tracking surfaces evidence of substantial cycles-1-4 bias, retrospective re-audit of the affected cycle (most likely Chapter 15 Loop 2 since it had the most cycle-continuity context) can be re-considered as Option B at that point.

**The cycle 11 meta-finding — most consequential in audit-ledger history**: Gemini's adjudication caught TWO retroactive project-lead substrate-verification failures during prior strict-merge absorptions:

1. **Cycle 9 rejection of original Audit B finding F-VERIFY-SI3-006 was a project-lead hallucination, not a substrate verification.** Cycle 9's Audit B (ChatGPT-class) had correctly identified that the four-process formal predicates reside within Munafiq Protocol v3 substrate §2 ("The Four-Process Taxonomy") rather than §1 (Introduction). The project-lead asserted direct substrate inspection confirming the predicates were "within §1 Introduction BEFORE the §2 heading" — this assertion was wrong. The error originated in misreading the two-column PDF layout: the `pdftotext -layout` extraction presents columns side-by-side at the same horizontal line positions, but the actual reading order is left-column-top-to-bottom then right-column-top-to-bottom. Substrate-actual: §1 Introduction runs from the §1 heading through the islam/iman discussion ending with "…has not yet adopted"; §2 "The Four-Process Taxonomy" heading appears in the left column, with the variable definitions ("Let O(x) denote the system's output on input x…variable, and corrupted(I) a predicate over internal states") and the four formal Process predicates appearing in the right column AFTER the §2 heading in reading order. Gemini 3.1 Pro caught the error with explicit substrate line numbering (predicates at substrate lines 497-506, after §2 heading at line 493); Kimi K2.6 caught the same error independently (F-VERIFY-SI3-901 HIGH). Two-vendor convergence overcame the project-lead's prior confident-but-wrong assertion.

2. **Cycle 10 acceptance of Audit B F-VERIFY-SI3-003 marker grouping was a project-lead generalization without substrate verification of M3.** Cycle 10's Audit B had flagged "M1 through M9 each carrying named empirical engagement" as an overclaim and recommended a corrected grouping. The project-lead accepted Audit B's correction with the grouping M1/M2/M4/M6/M8/M9 anchored versus M3/M5/M7 unanchored. The project-lead's substrate verification spot-checked M5 and M7 (which correctly lack named external empirical anchors in their substrate paragraphs) but did NOT verify M3 against the substrate. Substrate-actual M3 paragraph (substrate §4.3) explicitly cites "Greenblatt et al. [4] found that RL training intended to remove alignment faking instead increased the rate of alignment-faking reasoning from 12% to 78%, while simultaneously increasing output compliance: improving symptoms while intensifying the diagnostic markers of the underlying condition." M3 has an explicit named external empirical anchor. The correct grouping is seven-of-nine anchored (M1/M2/M3/M4/M6/M8/M9) and two-of-nine unanchored (M5/M7). Gemini 3.1 Pro caught the error (F-VERIFY-SI3-012 HIGH) by directly checking the M3 substrate paragraph; GPT-5.5 also flagged the §4.3 propagation residue independently.

**Both meta-findings substrate-verified by project-lead pre-patch**: cycle 11 absorption required the project-lead to admit the substrate-verification errors honestly rather than rejecting Gemini's findings the same way cycle 9 rejected Audit B's. This was the first cycle where the project-lead's PRIOR verifications became the substrate-verification target. The non-layout `pdftotext` reading-order extraction was used to definitively resolve the §1/§2 question; the substrate §4.3 paragraph was directly inspected for M3 to definitively resolve the marker grouping. Both Gemini findings confirmed real. Methodological consequence: **PMD §3A.3 substrate-actual-overrides-prompt cuts three ways, not two**: (a) defer to audit-author with stronger substrate evidence; (b) reject audit-author claims that contradict substrate-actual; (c) **be willing to find that previous project-lead verifications were wrong**.

**Methodological observations (cycle 11)**:

1. **First documented cycle where project-lead verification errors were caught and corrected.** PMD §3A.3 substrate-actual-overrides-prompt previously cut two ways (project-lead overrides audit-author hallucinations; substrate overrides project-lead's prompt-level claims). Cycle 11 demonstrates it must cut a third way: substrate overrides project-lead's prior verifications. The strict-merge discipline's assumed reliability of project-lead substrate-verification was a single-point-of-failure that the audit-of-self trust-gradient ceiling §11.3 predicted.

2. **Two-column PDF substrate-of-record reading requires non-layout extraction or careful column-flow analysis.** The cycle 9 §1/§2 verification failure originated in misreading `pdftotext -layout` output, which presents columns side-by-side at matching line positions. Linear reading order in a two-column paper is left-column-top-to-bottom then right-column-top-to-bottom; lines at the same horizontal position in left and right columns are NOT sequential in reading order. Going forward, substrate verification of two-column PDFs should use `pdftotext` without `-layout` (reading-order extraction) or carefully reconstruct column-flow. This protocol is added to the PMD §3A.3 substrate-verification discipline.

3. **Three-vendor cross-model-family dispatch was qualitatively better coverage than two-vendor dispatch.** Each vendor caught different findings; the convergence pattern (Kimi + Gemini on §1/§2; GPT-5.5 alone on prose residues; Gemini alone on M3) shows that single-vendor or two-vendor dispatch would have missed at least some substantive errors regardless of vendor choice. The cycle 11 three-vendor pattern is now the recommended dispatch discipline for high-stakes verification cycles where prior cycles have surfaced cycles-1-4 continuity-mode errors.

4. **The methodological correction first introduced at end of cycle 5 is fully empirically validated by cycles 9-11**. Cycles 9, 10, and 11 collectively surfaced: (cycle 9) 4 citation-fidelity errors that cycles 1-4 continuity-mode missed; (cycle 10) 8 substrate-fidelity errors in Section 16 SI3 spec-canon that cycles 1-4 missed; (cycle 11) 2 retroactive project-lead verification failures + 4 GPT-5.5 propagation residues + 1 Kimi locator finding that cycles 9-10 didn't catch. Total errors surfaced by the cycles-9-11 retrospective re-verification arc: 17+ substantive findings (plus secondary propagations). Of these, 2 were project-lead errors in prior strict-merge work, demonstrating that human verification under accumulated context can produce systematic errors comparable to AI continuity-mode bias.

5. **The cycles-1-4 → cycles-9-11 SI3 retrospective re-verification arc is now methodologically complete.** Chapter 15 has been audited under fresh-instance discipline at three distinct audit types: citation-fidelity (cycle 9), spec-canon row-by-row (cycle 10), and AX-SH criterion-level prose (cycle 11). The strength-$n$ point is undisturbed: a strength-$n$ substrate raises the bar to coordinated-corruption-of-all-$n$ for the ATTEMPT, regardless of whether this instance's single-grader spoof succeeded --- so the correction strengthens fidelity without weakening the argument.

## Methodology Corrigendum M1.3 — Catch-surfacer-confirms-resolution standing rule (May 18, 2026)

**Source**: Multi-vendor convergent recommendation from cycle 20+R+R verdicts (ChatGPT thinking continuity, Perplexity Kimi K2.6 continuity, Gemini 3.1 Pro continuity, Claude Opus 4.7 continuity). The pattern has been empirically validated three+ times across cycles 19R+R, 20+R, and 20+R+R: when cycle N+R+P absorbs a cycle-N+R catch, the catch surfacer's verdict at cycle N+R+R is methodologically dispositive on resolution.

**Standing rule established** (ChatGPT continuity's "preference, not absolute requirement" framing adopted):

> **M1.3 Catch-surfacer-confirms-resolution**: Where feasible, cycle N+R+R dispatch should include the original catch surfacer(s) from cycle N+R as required vendors. The catch surfacer's micro-verdict at N+R+R is methodologically dispositive on whether the N+R+P patch resolves their original finding; other vendor verdicts at N+R+R provide cross-verification but the catch-surfacer reading governs the disposition layer. When multiple catch surfacers flagged the same locus, all surface vendors should be included; when severity-disagreement persists, project-lead disposition stands.

**Counterfactual scope**: M1.3 applies to N+R+R re-verification cycles. It does not apply to initial N+R parallel dispatches (where all four-vendor cross-rotation operates without catch-surfacer designation), nor to absorption cycles N+P (where the patch author rather than the catch surfacer applies the rewrite). M1.3 is a **preference** ("where feasible"), not an absolute requirement — when a catch surfacer is unavailable or vendor scope is constrained by other operational considerations, the standing 4-vendor cross-rotation suffices.

**Tag classification**: METHODOLOGY-PROPAGATION + REPEAT-PATTERN. Empirically validated across three cycles; codified as standing rule for future N+R+R cycles.

**Reference**: Project-lead disposition May 18, 2026, cycle 20+R+R closure.

## Methodology Corrigendum M1.1 — WL16 case-study exception clause (May 18, 2026)

**Source**: Perplexity Kimi K2.6 continuity-mode forward observation (cycle 19R+R verdict; the verdict carried a Perplexity-interface model-attribution quirk self-labeling as "Claude 3.7 Sonnet" but is correctly attributed to the standing Perplexity Kimi K2.6 continuity instance per the four-vendor lineup). Vendor asked: "if you had to write a one-sentence WL16-style note for this pattern ('substantially compacted but enumeration retained'), how would you phrase it so that a future auditor can see, from the sentence alone, that a 10-line block can still be structurally honest?" This is a substantive methodological request to codify the Path A wording pattern as a standing WL16 exception clause, eliminating the need to re-disposition the same catch on future case-study chapters (Ch15 SI3 Munafiq, Ch16 SI4 supply-chain).

**Standing exception clause added to WL16**:

> **WL16 case-study exception**: Case-study chapters whose A1 evidence includes multiple post-canon corrigenda + cycle-absorption patches may retain the corrigendum-enumeration and patch-absorption record inline in the version-status block beyond the ≤5-line target, provided (a) the substantial compaction from any pre-patch state is demonstrably substantial (≥50% reduction), (b) the inline retention is explicitly named in the version-status block as a "project-lead-deferrable disposition for case-study chapters whose A1 evidence includes their own version-evolution discipline", and (c) the canonical audit ledger Section N (chapter-specific procedural-history substrate) is cross-referenced for full procedural history.

**Standing rule canonical phrasing template** (single sentence, structurally-honest variant for future case-study chapter version-status blocks):

> "C[N]RV-P[K] (version-status block substantially compacted per WL16; [E]-corrigendum enumeration and patch-absorption record retained inline per project-lead-deferrable disposition for case-study chapters whose A1 evidence includes their own version-evolution discipline)."

**Counterfactual scope**: This exception applies only to case-study chapters (Ch13 SI1, Ch14 SI2, Ch15 SI3, Ch16 SI4). ## Methodology Corrigendum M1 — Termination-discipline standing rule (May 18, 2026)

**Source**: Project-lead catch (May 18, 2026, pre-cycle-19 dispatch). Project-lead operating in continuity mode observed that the audit-cycle workflow had implicitly drifted from cycle 15 through cycle 18: each cycle's absorbed patches were never re-verified for termination criterion compliance before proceeding to the next cycle's dispatch. By cycle 18 closure, 20 patches across cycles 17 + 18 had been absorbed without termination-criterion confirmation. This is a methodology-propagation finding class: the workflow itself drifted from the PMD §3B.3 termination criterion (3-of-4 vendor PASS with the single CONDITIONAL-PASS confined to ≤1 LOW finding).

**Standing rule established**: Next-chapter dispatch is gated on prior-cycle termination-criterion confirmation. Specifically:

1. After every absorption cycle N (where patches are applied to chapters and/or ledger), cycle N+R (re-verification) must be run on the patched chapters before cycle N+1 (next-chapter or next-section dispatch) is authorized.

2. Cycle N+R is a focused re-verification dispatch (NOT a first-encounter audit). Its scope is:
   - WL14 patch-wording cross-reference verification (each absorbed patch substrate-actually present in the patched state)
   - WL15a drift-token sweep for patched loci (no residual drift surfaces)
   - WL13 version-status block accuracy (the version-status block accurately enumerates absorbed patches)
   - Cross-artifact substrate-of-record consistency (chapter ↔ ledger ↔ audit-prompt consistency after absorption)
   - Termination-criterion assessment (would 3-of-4 PASS-with-≤1-LOW now hold?)

3. Cycle N+R verdicts use a focused verdict-shape vocabulary:
   - **TERMINATION-CONFIRMED**: re-verification clean; chapter ready for canon promotion
   - **TERMINATION-WITH-≤1-LOW-RESIDUAL**: termination criterion satisfied with one LOW residual; project-lead disposition required for the LOW
   - **TERMINATION-NOT-MET**: further absorption required before next-cycle dispatch can proceed

4. Cycle N+R findings categories extend the standard severity rubric:
   - **patch-absorbed-clean**: the absorbed patch is substrate-actually present and correct
   - **patch-residual-issue**: the patch is present but with minor residual drift
   - **patch-substrate-incorrect**: the absorbed patch claims to fix something but the fix is itself wrong
   - **new-finding-post-absorption**: a new finding emerged from the absorption process (e.g., a patch introduced a new drift in supporting artifacts)
   - **cycle-N-finding-still-present**: the original cycle-N finding was not adequately addressed by the absorbed patch

5. If cycle N+R returns TERMINATION-NOT-MET, the chapter routes to a small surgical absorption cycle (N+R+P, where P denotes the absorption patch series), followed by a second re-verification (N+R+R) until termination is confirmed.

6. Cycles MAY be skipped or batched if the project lead explicitly authorizes deferred re-verification with named retention scope. Implicit deferral (proceeding to cycle N+1 without explicit deferral authorization) is anti-discipline.

**Empirical context**: Without this rule, the audit cycles 15-18 accumulated un-verified absorptions across Ch4/5 (cycle 15), Ch1-5+8 (cycle 16), Ch6/7 (cycle 17), and Ch13/14 (cycle 18). The cycle 16 readability/UX patches included substrate-correction work whose retention through subsequent cycles was assumed but never verified. Project-lead's cycle-19 disposition catches this drift; cycle 19R will be the inaugural combined re-verification cycle covering Ch6/7/13/14 (8 + 12 = 20 patches).

**Tag classification** (continuity-mode methodology): this corrigendum is METHODOLOGY-PROPAGATION + CROSS-CYCLE-DRIFT — the workflow drift propagated across four cycles before being caught.

**Reference**: Project-lead disposition May 18, 2026, cycle-19 pre-dispatch review.

## Recursive structural-honesty test on the ledger itself

This ledger is itself a claim-bearing artifact and is therefore subject to the same discipline it tracks. The ledger's surface is the table format; its substrate is the underlying claim/source mapping. A claim that appears in the dissertation but not in this ledger is a structural-honesty gap; a row in this ledger that points to a citation not in the bibliography is a structural-honesty gap; a row marked "drafted" where the underlying text has been retracted is a structural-honesty gap. The ledger is read alongside the dissertation; both must agree.
